title: Office Furniture Installation Newcastle: What Must Be Included Before Move-In?
metaTitle: Office Furniture Installation Newcastle: Checklist | YOS
metaDescription: Plan office furniture installation in Newcastle, NSW. Confirm delivery access, assembly, placement, packaging removal, defects and handover before staff move in.
excerpt: Delivered is not the same as ready to use. Agree the installation scope, site access and handover responsibilities before your Newcastle office furniture arrives.
body:
Office furniture installation in Newcastle should have an agreed scope for delivery access, assembly, placement, packaging removal and handover checks. Confirm who handles existing furniture and any separate power or data work. Do not assume a delivery price covers everything required for staff to use the office.

For a furniture-only refresh, this may be a focused supplier installation. For a wider NSW workplace FitOut, it needs coordination with the building work, services and occupation requirements. The furniture handover is one part of business readiness, not proof that every project condition has been satisfied.

## What should a furniture installation quote include?

Ask the supplier to describe the outcome, not just the word installation. Record whether the products arrive assembled, what is assembled on site and who positions the furniture to the approved layout.

| Scope item | Question to settle before ordering |
| --- | --- |
| Delivery | Where will the vehicle unload, and who books the access? |
| Handling | Are lifts, stairs, floor protection and large items covered? |
| Assembly | Which products need assembly, and who performs it? |
| Placement | Is room-by-room positioning to the approved layout included? |
| Fixing | Are any fixings required, and who confirms permissions and suitability? |
| Existing furniture | Who dismantles, moves, stores or removes it? |
| Packaging | Who clears and removes wrapping, pallets and cartons? |
| Services | What must an IT provider or appropriately qualified trade do separately? |
| Handover | Who inspects, records defects and arranges outstanding actions? |

A quote with unresolved access or assembly charges is not yet a complete installed price.

[Compare furniture quotes on an equivalent installed scope](/blog/compare-office-furniture-quotes-installed-cost)

## Check Newcastle building access before booking delivery

Send the supplier the complete site address, floor, contact and measured route from unloading to installation. Ask building management about bookings, vehicle access, lift dimensions, access cards, permitted work windows and protection of common areas.

A Newcastle CBD tenancy can have different requirements from a ground-floor Hunter office. An office in Wickham, Hamilton, Charlestown or Maitland still needs its own access review; the suburb alone does not tell you whether a delivery will work.

Confirm which party obtains any necessary permission for the proposed unloading arrangement. Do not plan to obstruct a public footpath or use restricted access simply because the truck is booked. Resolve arrangements with the appropriate building or public authority where required.

## Agree the installation sequence

Confirm when the relevant rooms and access route will be ready. In a wider FitOut, that includes coordinating with the appointed team responsible for the building works and services. Avoid scheduling furniture solely against an optimistic completion date.

For an occupied office, identify which teams or rooms need to remain operational. Agree staged work, staff access and any after-hours scope before comparing quotes. Repeated visits may affect the cost and program.

Keep retained furniture in the plan. If new products cannot be placed until old workstations are dismantled, assign that task and confirm its timing.

[Audit retained furniture before a Newcastle office move](/blog/office-furniture-reuse-audit-newcastle)

## Separate furniture assembly from power and data work

A desk can be assembled while its equipment is not ready for use. Identify who installs or connects the intended power, data and IT systems, and distinguish supplier accessories from work requiring a qualified trade.

Do not assume a furniture crew can alter building wiring or certify a workplace. The appropriate professionals must confirm the requirements for the actual scope. If works extend beyond furniture replacement, establish any landlord permissions and planning or certification requirements before proceeding.

Service NSW explains that approval pathways depend on the proposed development and its eligibility. Check with the relevant council or accredited certifier where building changes require assessment; a checklist cannot determine the pathway for your project.

[Service NSW: checking eligibility for a complying development certificate](https://www.service.nsw.gov.au/transaction/apply-for-a-complying-development-certificate)

## Inspect the installed settings before staff arrive

Compare installed quantities, models and finishes with the approved schedule. Check positioning against the agreed layout and record visible damage or incomplete assembly for the supplier to resolve.

Have the installer confirm assembly and any relevant fixing requirements. Check that chairs and adjustable settings are explained to users and that instructions are provided. Escalate suitability or safety concerns to the appropriate people rather than accepting a photograph as handover evidence.

Test a normal working day with the people responsible for IT and workplace operation. Can staff access the space, use the intended setting and reach the equipment they need? Furniture completion and working technology need coordinated checks.

## Agree what happens to packaging and cleaning

Packaging removal and cleaning are different tasks. Confirm who removes cartons, pallets and protective wrapping, then establish who deals with installation dust or any construction-related clean.

Do not expect an ongoing cleaner to absorb a large unplanned clearance. For eligible Newcastle CBD and Lake Macquarie workplaces, YOS commercial cleaning can be considered under an agreed scope. Confirm coverage and requirements rather than assuming every NSW furniture project includes a clean.

[Discuss commercial cleaning requirements](/cleaning#cleaning-quote-form)

## Create a handover and defects register

Record each issue, the responsible supplier or contractor, its priority and the agreed completion date. Separate matters that prevent safe or approved use from those the responsible parties agree can be resolved later.

| Handover record | Detail to keep |
| --- | --- |
| Installed schedule | Quantities, model codes, finishes and locations |
| Instructions and warranty | Applicable assembly, use and maintenance information |
| Outstanding work | Clear action, owner, date and impact on occupation |
| Support | Named supplier contact and process for reporting defects |
| Completion evidence | Inspection notes, agreed acceptance and relevant supporting records |

Do not let a removalist booking decide whether a room or workplace can be used. The relevant project professionals must assess unresolved conditions.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does office furniture delivery include assembly in Newcastle?

Only if agreed in the proposal. Confirm assembly, placement, access, packaging and any separate charges for the actual site.

### Can installation happen while the office is occupied?

It may be possible with an appropriate staged plan. Agree access, work areas, operational restrictions and timing with the responsible parties before booking.

### Who connects equipment after the desks are installed?

Allocate IT and trade tasks separately. Ask the appropriate provider to confirm what work is needed and who is authorised to perform it.

### Is furniture handover the same as permission to occupy?

No. Applicable approvals, services and occupation requirements depend on the project. Furniture handover is one workstream within that wider process.
